name: Queue consumer
purpose: Take messages off a queue and hand each one to a job handler, owning acknowledgement and delivery semantics.
responsibilities: Subscribe to or poll the queue and pull messages
Deserialise and validate the message payload before handing it on
Invoke the job handler with a typed payload
Acknowledge on success and negatively acknowledge or dead-letter on failure
Translate broker-specific delivery events into a uniform outcome
restrictions: Must NOT contain business logic — it delegates, it does not decide
Must NOT create, declare or configure queue infrastructure
Must NOT re-enqueue its own retries; retry and backoff are broker policy owned by the queue manager
Must NOT acknowledge a message whose handler threw
Must NOT assume a message is delivered exactly once

interface.errorHandling: A handler throwing is a negative acknowledgement. The consumer never converts a failure into a silent success.

gracefulShutdown.description: On shutdown, stop accepting new messages, wait for in-flight handlers to finish within a bounded timeout, then close the connection. A consumer killed mid-message must leave that message unacknowledged so it redelivers.
gracefulShutdown.example: await consumer.stop(); // stops intake, awaits in-flight, closes

payloadValidation.description: Validate the deserialised payload before the handler sees it. A malformed message is a poison message and belongs in the dead-letter queue, not in a retry loop.

agentHints: The consumer is thin. If it is making decisions about the work, that logic belongs in the job handler.
Take the queue connection by injection — never construct it here.
A message that fails validation is not retryable. Dead-letter it rather than throwing into the retry path.
Bound concurrency explicitly; the broker default is rarely the right number for the downstream dependency.
